div.head: II Cn 19
div.ab: And ne níme nán man nane næme ne innan scire ne ut of scire, ær mann hæbbe þriwa on hundrede his rihtes gebeden.
Be nááme. ⁊ ne nime nan man nane náme ne inne scire ne ut of scire, ær man hæbbe rihtes gebeden.
And ne nime nan man náme ne innan scyran ne ut of scyre, ær man habbe þrywa on hundrode his rihtes gebedan.
quam ter in hundreto suo rectum sibi perquisierit. Et nemo námum capiat in comitatu uel extra comitatum, prius-
uocant náme nec infra comitatum nec extra, antequam ter iusticiam in hundredo requirat. Nullus accipiat pro aliqua forisfactura quicquam quod Angli
extra comitatum, nisi primum ter postulauerit suum rectum in suo centenario. Neque capiat quisquam captionem neque intra comitatum neque
Be nááme. ⁊ ne nime nan man nane náme ne inne scire ne ut of scire, ær man hæbbe [þriwa on hundrede his] rihtes gebeden.
And ne nime nan man nane næme, ne innan scire ne ut of scire, ær mann hæbbe þriwa on hundrede his rihtes gebeden.

(Vom Pfand. B) Und niemand nehme ein Pfand [für Urtheilserfüllung dem Processgegner fort], weder innerhalb des Grafschaftsgerichts noch aussergerichtlich, bevor er im Hundertschafts[gericht] sein Recht dreimal [vergeblich] gefordert hat.

(Of distraint. B) And let no one take a distress [from his opponent to enforce a judgment], either within the shire[-court] or outside the shire, until he has three times asked for his right [in vain] in the hundred[-court].
Concerning distraint of property. And no-one shall make distraint of property either within the shire or outside it, until he has appealed for justice [three times in the hundred court].
And no one is to distrain on property either within the shire or outside it until he has demanded his rights three times in the hundred.
And no one shall execute a legal repossession of property, either within or outside the shire, until he has brought his claim to the hundred court three times.

Geographische Bed. nimmt Toller scir III an; vielleicht auch Schmid 642, dagegen ‘shiregemot’ Bigelow Hist. proced. 205. Vgl. 19, 2²; Gl Grafschaftsgericht 4. Jene dachten wohl an das Forttreiben von Vieh über die Grafschaftsgrenze, was den Gepfändeten mehr benachteiligt als ein Pfänden in der Nachbarschaft, das Auslösung leichter ermöglicht

Toller scir III assumes a geographical meaning; perhaps Schmid 642 too; on the other hand ‘shiregemot’ Bigelow Hist. proced. 205. Cf. 19, 2²; Gl Grafschaftsgericht 4. The former were probably thinking of the driving of cattle across the county boundary, which disadvantages the distrainee more than a distraint in the neighbourhood, which makes redemption easier
